name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district lean in North Dakota
Fedorchak is a well-funded incumbent with $1.05M on hand
Hammer's fundraising is minimal ($190K raised, $67K cash)
model.rationale: The R+18 baseline, incumbent advantage, and a 10-to-1 fundraising gap all point to a safe Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at ~96% Republican. No polling or expert ratings justify moving materially from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Hammer or a sudden statewide Democratic environment shift could move this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+18. Republican Julie Fedorchak, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and holds a large financial advantage, with about $1.06 million on hand compared with roughly $67,000 for Democrat Trygve Hammer. No independent or third-party candidates appear competitive.

There is no public general-election polling and no expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets. Polymarket prices Democratic chances at about 3 percent. The baseline model puts the expected Republican margin near 17 points, and the evidence supports treating this as a safe Republican hold with high confidence.
